methodology_note: Scanned all 97 chapter JSON files (chapter_notes + section_notes + chapter_subheading_notes) for 17 positive-restriction regex patterns. Initial scan yielded 286 hits; after dedup and manual semantic analysis, 24 chapter/heading-level rules were extracted as TRUE positive-restriction notes (closed definitions, no escape hatch in the operative clause). Sub-heading-only restrictions (e.g., Ch.17 1701.13, Ch.84 8482.40, Ch.85 8525.81/8527.12) were SKIPPED because chapter_exclusions is a chapter/heading-routing table — sub-heading granularity is too fine. 'Pellets' definitions across Section IV chapters (06-24) were SKIPPED as they are stipulative quantitative definitions (binder ≤3% by weight), not restrictive of competing chapters. 'Insert all 17 occurrences of cermets' was reduced to 1 canonical rule on the source chapter (Ch.72) since it is a Section-XV-wide definition; the same applies to base metals (Ch.72) and machine/electrical-electronic-waste (Ch.84/85). Skipped: 'high-tenacity yarn' / 'textile garments' / 'made up' / 'put up for retail sale' / 'impregnated includes dipped' / 'polyamides includes aramids' — these are linguistic-clarifying definitions for Section XI sub-classification within textiles, NOT chapter-routing exclusions. Skipped: 'Brix value', 'unladen weight', 'pocket-size', 'machining centres' subheading scopes — sub-heading qualifiers. Skipped: anything with 'inter alia', 'such as', 'etc.', 'and the like', 'and similar', 'for example' INSIDE the operative restrictive clause (open lists). Kept only when these phrases appear in optional context (e.g., parenthetical for one item) and the principal list is closed.
dedup_check_results: Queried existing chapter_exclusions for collisions on (source_chapter, source_note_number) for all 32 candidate notes. 2 collisions found and SKIPPED: (a) Ch.43 Note 5 — already covered by 2 existing rules redirecting woven/knitted imitation furs → 5801/6001. (b) Ch.70 Note 4 — already covered by an existing rule for 'mineral wools not meeting glass-wool spec → 6806'. The remaining 30 proposed inserts are NEW (no collision on the (chapter, note_number, exclusion_text) tuple).

self_spot_check.exclusion_text: imitation, synthetic, artificial or composition 'leather' of plastics, textile, rubber or other non-hide materials — Ch.42 Note 1 limits 'leather' to chamois, patent, patent-laminated, metallised, and (by extension via heading 4115) composition leather of real hide fibre
self_spot_check.source_note_excerpt: For the purposes of this Chapter, the term 'leather' includes chamois (including combination chamois) leather, patent leather, patent laminated leather and metallised leather.
self_spot_check.why_this_is_restrictive: The note enumerates the four sub-types of 'leather' that fall in Ch.42 with NO escape hatch on the principal list ('and metallised leather' terminates the enumeration). The parenthetical '(including combination chamois)' qualifies one item only and is not an open-extension of the principal list. WCO HS Explanatory Notes consistently interpret 'the term X includes A, B, C, D' (closed enumeration) as a definition by restriction. This is the seed case identified in the Phase 3 architecture spike (case-8 synthetic-leather PU sheet → Ch.39 not Ch.42) — the spike report explicitly flags this as RULES_GAP.

self_spot_check.exclusion_text: non-made-up knitted or crocheted fabrics, piece goods, and woven (non-knitted) garments
self_spot_check.source_note_excerpt: This Chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles.
self_spot_check.why_this_is_restrictive: Two co-restrictions in 11 words: (i) only MADE UP, (ii) only KNITTED OR CROCHETED. Anything that is woven (non-knitted) → Ch.62. Anything that is not yet made up (piece goods) → Chapters 50-60. No escape hatch.

self_spot_check.exclusion_text: knitted or crocheted articles, wadding articles, and non-made-up woven piece goods
self_spot_check.source_note_excerpt: This Chapter applies only to made up articles of any textile fabric other than wadding, excluding knitted or crocheted (other than those of heading 6212).
self_spot_check.why_this_is_restrictive: Tight restriction: only made-up + not wadding + not knitted/crocheted (with one heading-6212 carve-out). The carve-out for heading 6212 is an EXPLICIT named exception, not an open hatch. Knitted articles redirect to Ch.61; wadding goods to Ch.56.

self_spot_check.exclusion_text: tools/cutlery whose blade or working part is NOT base metal, metal carbides/cermets, precious stones on supporting metal, or abrasive material on base metal — e.g., all-plastic, ceramic-only, or wooden working tools
self_spot_check.source_note_excerpt: Apart from blow lamps, portable forges, grinding wheels with frameworks, manicure or pedicure sets, and goods of heading 8209, this Chapter covers only articles with a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of: (a) base metal; (b) metal carbides or cermets; (c) precious or semi-precious stones (natural, synthetic or reconstructed) on a support of base metal, metal carbide or cermet; or (d) abrasive materials on a support of base metal...
self_spot_check.why_this_is_restrictive: Explicit 'covers only' restricting Ch.82 to tools whose working part is one of 4 enumerated material classes. The carve-out for 5 named items at the front ('Apart from ... blow lamps, portable forges...') is a closed exception, not an open hatch. Tools of ceramic working part → Ch.69; of plastic → Ch.39; of wood → Ch.44.

self_spot_check.exclusion_text: watches with case NOT of precious metal or precious-metal-clad or those materials with pearls/gem stones — e.g., steel, plastic, base-metal-inlaid watches
self_spot_check.source_note_excerpt: Heading 9101 covers only watches with case wholly of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal, or of the same materials combined with natural or cultured pearls, or precious or semi-precious stones (natural, synthetic or reconstructed) of headings 7101 to 7104. Watches with case of base metal inlaid with precious metal fall in heading 9102.
self_spot_check.why_this_is_restrictive: Explicit 'covers only' with closed material list, and a redirect rule for base-metal-inlaid watches → 9102. Anything else (steel, plastic case) → 9102. This is one of the false-anchor traps the spike report flagged for Ch.91.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: imitation, synthetic, artificial or composition 'leather' of plastics, textile, rubber or non-hide materials — Ch.42 'leather' is restricted to chamois (incl. combination chamois) leather, patent leather, patent-laminated leather, and metallised leather
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the term 'leather' includes chamois (including combination chamois) leather, patent leather, patent laminated leather and metallised leather.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Ch.42 Note 1 defines 'leather' by closed enumeration (4 sub-types). Plastic-based imitation leather (PU/PVC sheet) → Ch.39 (3920/3921). Textile-backed imitation leather → Ch.59 (5903). This is the explicit gap identified in Phase 3 spike case-8.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: minerals/products of Ch.25 that have been roasted, calcined, obtained by mixing, or processed beyond what each heading allows — e.g., calcined alumina (heading 2818), mixed mineral preparations
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Except where their context or Note 4 to this Chapter otherwise requires, the headings of this Chapter cover only products which are in the crude state or which have been washed, crushed, ground, powdered, levigated, sifted, screened, concentrated by flotation, magnetic separation or other mechanical or physical processes (except crystallization), but not products that have been roasted, calcined, obtained by mixing or subjected to processing beyond that mentioned in each heading.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Ch.25 Note 1 is the textbook 'covers only' chapter-level restriction. Processed minerals (calcined, roasted, mixed) leave Ch.25 — typically → Ch.28 (inorganic chemicals) or Ch.68 (articles of stone).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: ore-like materials of headings 2601-2617 that are NOT minerals actually used in the metallurgical industry for extraction of mercury, of metals of heading 2844, or of metals of Sections XIV/XV, AND ores that have been submitted to processes not normal to the metallurgical industry
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of headings 2601 to 2617, the term 'ores' means minerals of mineralogical species actually used in the metallurgical industry for the extraction of mercury, of the metals of heading 2844 or of the metals of Section XIV or XV, even if they are intended for nonmetallurgical purposes. Headings 2601 to 2617 do not, however, include minerals which have been submitted to processes not normal to the metallurgical industry.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Ch.26 Note 2 'the term ores means' restricts 'ores' to a metallurgically-defined set. The second sentence is an explicit cross-out for processed minerals — redirect to Ch.25 (unprocessed minerals) or Ch.28 (chemically-defined compounds).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: slag/ash/residues NOT of a kind used in industry for metal extraction OR for the manufacture of metal chemical compounds — e.g., ash and residues from incineration of municipal waste
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 2620 applies only to: (a) slag, ash and residues of a kind used in industry either for the extraction of metals or as a basis for the manufacture of chemical compounds of metals, excluding ash and residues from the incineration of municipal waste (heading 2621); and (b) slag, ash and residues containing arsenic, whether or not containing metals, of a kind used either for the extraction of arsenic or metals or for the manufacture of their chemical compounds.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Ch.26 Note 3 'applies only to' restricts heading 2620 with explicit named redirect (municipal-waste ash → 2621). Closed 2-clause list.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: oxygen-containing characteristic groups in headings 2911/2912/2914/2918/2922 that are NOT the oxygen functions referenced in headings 2905-2920
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of headings 2911, 2912, 2914, 2918 and 2922, 'oxygen function', the characteristic organic oxygen-containing group of those respective headings, is restricted to the oxygen-functions referred to in headings 2905 to 2920.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Explicit 'is restricted to'. Internal Ch.29 sub-classification restriction — no clean cross-chapter redirect, but documents the rule for organic-chemistry routing within Ch.29.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: nitrogenous fertilisers NOT in heading 3105 forms, AND not one of the 8 enumerated mineral compounds (sodium/ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, urea, calcium cyanamide, etc.) NOR mixtures/solutions of these
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 3102 applies only to the following goods, provided that they are not put up in the forms or packages described in heading 3105: (a) goods which answer to one or other of the descriptions given below: (i) sodium nitrate, whether or not pure; (ii) ammonium nitrate, whether or not pure; (iii) double salts, whether or not pure, of ammonium sulphate and ammonium nitrate; (iv) ammonium sulphate, whether or not pure; (v) double salts (whether or not pure) or mixtures of calcium nitrate and ammonium nitrate; (vi) double salts (whether or not pure) or mixtures of calciumnitrate and magnesiumnitrate; (vii) calcium cyanamide, whether or not pure or treated with oil; (viii) urea, whether or not pure; (b) fertilisers consisting of any of the goods described in (A) above mixed together; (c) fertilisers consisting of ammonium chloride or of any of the goods described in (A) or (B) above mixed with chalk, gypsumor other inorganic non-fertilising substances; (d) liquid fertilisers consisting of the goods of sub-paragraph (A) (ii) or (viii) above, or of mixtures of those goods, in an aqueous or ammoniacal solution.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Heading 3102 'applies only to' with 8 named compounds + their mixtures. Closed enumeration. Pure chemically-defined nitrogen compounds NOT on this list → Ch.28.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: phosphatic fertilisers in heading 3103 NOT in 3105 forms, AND not one of the 4 enumerated compounds (basic slag, calcined natural phosphates, superphosphates, calcium hydrogen orthophosphate) nor mixtures thereof
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 3103 applies only to the following goods, provided that they are not put up in the forms or packages described in heading 3105: (a) goods which answer to one or other of the descriptions given below: (i) basic slag; (ii) natural phosphates of heading 2510, calcined or further heat-treated than for the removal of impurities; (iii) super phosphates (single, double or triple); (iv) calcium hydrogen orthophosphate containing not less than 0.2 per cent. by weight of fluorine calculated on the dry anhydrous product; (b) fertilisers consisting of any of the goods described in (A) above mixed together; (c) fertilisers consisting of any of the goods described in (A) or (B) above, but with no account being taken of the flourine content limit, mixed with chalk, gypsum or other inorganic nonfertilising substances.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Heading 3103 'applies only to' parallels Note 2 — closed enumeration for phosphatic fertilisers. Pure phosphates not on this list → Ch.28.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: products in heading 3105 'other fertilisers' that do NOT contain at least one of N, P, or K as essential constituent
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of heading 3105, the term 'other fertilisers' applies only to products of a kind used as fertilisers and containing, as an essential constituent, at least one of the fertilising elements nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' restricts heading 3105 to N-P-K-containing fertilisers. Soil amendments with only Ca/Mg/micronutrients → Ch.28 (inorganic chemicals) or Ch.25 (mineral).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: products called 'waxes' in heading 3404 that are NOT (a) chemically produced organic waxy products, (b) mixtures of different waxes, or (c) products of waxy character with a basis of waxes — e.g., animal/vegetable unmixed waxes (1521), mineral waxes (2712), waxes dissolved in liquid (3405/3809)
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: In heading 3404, subject to the exclusions provided below, the expression 'artificial waxes and prepared waxes' applies only to: (a) chemically produced organic products of a waxy character, whether or not water-soluble; (b) products obtained by mixing different waxes; (c) products of a waxy character with a basis of one or more waxes and containing fats, resins, mineral substances or other materials. The heading does not apply to: (i) products of headings 1516, 3402 or 3823, even if having a waxy character; (ii) unmixed animal waxes or unmixed vegetable waxes, whether or not refined or coloured, of heading 1521; (iii) mineral waxes and similar products of heading 2712 whether or not intermixed or merely coloured; or (iv) waxes mixed with, dispersed in or dissolved in a liquid medium (headings 3405, 3809, etc.).
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with 3-item closed list AND explicit redirect rules for 4 exception classes. Heading 3404 boundary defined positively and the redirects explicit.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: biodiesel-like products in heading 3826 that are NOT mono-alkyl esters of fatty acids derived from animal/vegetable/microbial fats and oils used as fuel
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of heading 3826, the term 'biodiesel' means mono-alkyl esters of fatty acids of a kind used as a fuel, derived from animal or vegetable or microbial fats and oils whether or not used.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The term biodiesel means' closed chemical definition. Diesel/petroleum products → Ch.27; unmodified fats → Ch.15; pure FAME chemicals → Ch.29.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: products in headings 3920/3921 'plates, sheets, film, foil and strip' that are further worked beyond cutting into rectangles, or that are textile material of Chapter 54
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: In headings 3920 and 3921, the expression 'plates, sheets, film foil and strip' applies only to plates, sheets, film, foil and strip (other than those of Chapter 54) and to blocks of regular geometric shape, whether or not printed or otherwise surface-worked, uncut or cut into rectangles (including squares) but not further worked (even if when so cut they become articles ready for use).
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with closed shape-and-form restriction. Further-worked plastic articles → other Ch.39 headings (3923-3926). Plastic strip of Ch.54 → Ch.54. Note's parenthetical '(including squares)' qualifies 'rectangles' as a closed shape category — not an open hatch.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: rubber-like substances in heading 4002 that do NOT meet the vulcanisation-elongation-recovery test, OR thioplasts, OR specified modifications of natural rubber
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: In Note 1 to this Chapter and in heading 4002, the expression 'synthetic rubber' applies to: (a) unsaturated synthetic substances which can be irreversibly transformed by vulcanisation with sulphur into non-thermoplastic substances which, at a temperature between 180C and 290C, will not break on being extended to three times their original length and will return, after being extended to twice their original length, within a period of five minutes, to a length not greater than one and a half times their original length. For the purposes of this test, substances necessary for the cross-linking, such as vulcanising activators or accelerators, may be added; the presence of substances as provided for by Note 5(B)(ii) and (iii) is also permitted. However, the presence of any substances not necessary for the cross-linking, such as extenders, plasticisers and fillers, is not permitted; (b) thioplasts (TM); and (c) natural rubber modified by grafting or mixing with plastics, depolymerised natural rubber, mixtures of unsaturated synthetic substances with saturated synthetic high polymers provided that all the above-mentioned products comply with the requirements concerning vulcanisation, elongation and recovery in (a) above.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies to' followed by closed 3-clause definition with quantitative vulcanisation test. Polymers that FAIL the elasticity test → plastics (Ch.39). The 'such as' inside clause (a) qualifies which additives are permitted — it does NOT open the definition. The definition is gated by 'comply with the requirements'.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: wood subjected to ordinary lamination-only treatment (insufficient to acquire increased density/hardness or improved mechanical/chemical/electrical resistance) — NOT 'densified wood'
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: In this Chapter, the expression 'densified wood' means wood which has been subjected to chemical or physical treatment (being, in the case of layers bonded together, treatment in excess of that needed to ensure a good bond), and which has thereby acquired increased density or hardness together with improved mechanical strength or resistance to chemical or electrical agencies.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression densified wood means' with closed 2-criterion gate (treatment AND result). Internal Ch.44 sub-classification — no cross-chapter redirect, but documents what counts as 'densified' for heading 4413.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: wood pulp in heading 4702 that does NOT meet the quantitative dissolving-grade test (insoluble fraction thresholds: 92% for soda/sulphate, 88% for sulphite)
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of heading 4702, the expression 'chemical wood pulp, dissolving grades' means chemical wood pulp having by weight an insoluble fraction of 92% or more for soda or sulphate wood pulp or of 88% or more for sulphite wood pulp after one hour in a caustic soda solution containing 18% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at 20oC, and for sulphite wood pulp an ash content that does not exceed 0.15% by weight.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression X means' quantitative closed test. Pulp not meeting these thresholds → other Ch.47 headings (4703-4706 paper-grade pulps).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: products in Ch.57 in which textile materials do NOT serve as the exposed surface — e.g., wood/cork/rubber/plastic floor coverings with merely a textile underlay
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the term 'carpets and other textile floor coverings' means floor coverings in which textile materials serve as the exposed surface of the article when in use and includes articles having the characteristics of textile floor coverings but intended for use for other purposes.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The term X means' with closed gate (textile exposed surface). Floor coverings where the wear surface is NOT textile → respective material chapters (rubber 40, plastic 39, wood 44, cork 45, stone 68).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: fabrics referred to as 'textile fabrics' in Ch.59 that are NOT (a) woven fabrics of Ch.50-55 or headings 5803/5806, NOR (b) braids/trimmings of 5808, NOR (c) knitted/crocheted fabrics of 6002-6006 — e.g., nonwovens of 5603, tufted of 5802
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Except where the context otherwise requires, for the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'textile fabrics' applies only to the woven fabrics of Chapters 50 to 55 and headings 5803 and 5806, the braids and ornamental trimmings in the piece of heading 5808 and the knitted or crocheted fabrics of headings 6002 to 6006.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with 3-class closed list. Nonwovens / tufted carpets / felts are NOT 'textile fabrics' for Ch.59 — they redirect to Ch.56 (5603 nonwovens) or Ch.58 (5802 tufted).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: non-made-up knitted goods OR woven (non-knitted) garments — Ch.61 restricted to made-up KNITTED articles only
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: This Chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Compact 2-restriction. Non-made-up knitted fabrics → Ch.60. Woven garments → Ch.62. No escape hatch.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: knitted or crocheted garments (other than heading 6212), AND wadding articles, AND non-made-up textile piece goods
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: This Chapter applies only to made up articles of any textile fabric other than wadding, excluding knitted or crocheted (other than those of heading 6212).
proposed_inserts.rationale: Co-restriction: made-up + not wadding + not knitted (with named carve-out for 6212). Knitted → Ch.61. Wadding → Ch.56.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: non-made-up textile articles in Sub-Chapter I of Ch.63 (made-up products only)
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Sub-Chapter I applies only to made up articles, of any textile fabric.
proposed_inserts.rationale: Sub-Chapter scope restriction; non-made-up textile materials → respective textile chapters.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: second-hand textile or footwear/headgear goods in heading 6309 that do NOT meet BOTH conditions (appreciable wear AND bulk/bale presentation), OR articles outside the enumerated 6-class list
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 6309 applies only to the following goods: (a) articles of textile materials: (i) clothing and clothing accessories, and parts thereof; (ii) blankets and travelling rugs; (iii) bed linen, table linen, toilet linen and kitchen linen; (iv) furnishing articles, other than carpets of headings 5701 to 5705 and tapestries of heading 5805. (b) footwear and headgear of any material other than asbestos. In order to be classified in this heading, the articles mentioned above must comply with both of the following requirements: (i) they must show signs of appreciable wear, and (ii) they must be presented in bulk or in bales, sacks or similar packings.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with closed 2-class list AND closed 2-criterion gate (wear + bulk packaging). New textile articles → respective apparel chapters.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: products in Ch.69 that have NOT been fired after shaping — e.g., unfired clay tiles, green ceramic forms, articles heated below 800°C only for resin curing/dehydration
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: This Chapter applies only to ceramic products which have been fired after shaping: (a) headings 6904 to 6914 apply only to such products other than those classifiable in headings 6901 to 6903; (b) articles heated to temperatures less than 800C for purposes such as curing of resins, accelerating hydration reactions, or for the removal of water or other volatile components, are not considered to be fired. Such articles are excluded from Chapter 69.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with explicit quantitative threshold (>=800°C). Unfired ceramic blanks → Ch.25 (raw clays) or Ch.68 (articles of stone/asbestos/cement). The note explicitly says low-fired articles 'are excluded from Chapter 69'.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: tools, implements or cutlery in Ch.82 whose blade/working surface is NOT (a) base metal, (b) metal carbides/cermets, (c) precious/semi-precious stones on a metal-carbide/cermet support, or (d) abrasive material on a base-metal support — e.g., all-plastic, all-wood, or all-ceramic working tools
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Apart from blow lamps, portable forges, grinding wheels with frameworks, manicure or pedicure sets, and goods of heading 8209, this Chapter covers only articles with a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of: (a) base metal; (b) metal carbides or cermets; (c) precious or semi-precious stones (natural, synthetic or reconstructed) on a support of base metal, metal carbide or cermet; or (d) abrasive materials on a support of base metal, provided that the articles have cutting teeth, flutes, grooves, or the like, of base metal, which retain their identity and function after the application of the abrasive.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Covers only' with closed material list. Tools of plastic working part → Ch.39; wood → Ch.44; ceramic → Ch.69. The 'Apart from' clause names 5 explicit exceptions — closed, not open.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: electro-mechanical domestic appliances NOT meeting heading 8509 criteria — i.e., those over 20kg (except specifically named: polishers, food grinders/mixers, juice extractors) OR specifically listed redirect items (fans 8414, dryers 8421, dishwashers 8422, washing machines 8450, ironers 8420/8451, sewing 8452, electric scissors 8467, electrothermic 8516)
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 8509 covers only the following electro-mechanical machines of the kind commonly used for domestic purposes: (a) floor polishers, food grinders and mixers, and fruit or vegetable juice extractors, of any weight; (b) other machines provided the weight of such machines does not exceed 20 kg. The heading does not, however, apply to fans and ventilating or recycling hoods incorporating a fan, whether or not fitted with filters (heading 8414), centrifugal cloths-dryers (heading 8421), dishwashing machines (heading 8422), household washing machines (heading 8450), roller or other ironing machines (heading 8420 or 8451), sewing machines (heading 8452), electric scissors (heading 8467) or to electrothermic appliances (heading 8516).
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Covers only' with closed weight rule AND explicit named-heading redirects for 8 exception classes. Strong positive restriction with built-in heading map.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: remote-controlled or autonomous flying devices that are flying TOYS designed solely for amusement — NOT 'unmanned aircraft' under Ch.88
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'unmanned aircraft' means any aircraft, other than those of heading 8801, designed to be flown without a pilot on board. They may be designed to carry a payload or equipped with permanently integrated digital cameras or other equipment which would enable them to perform utilitarian functions during their flight. The expression 'unmanned aircraft', however, does not cover flying toys, designed solely for amusement purposes (heading 9503).
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression X means' with explicit exclusion-redirect inside the note: toy drones → 9503. Quad/hex copter drones with cameras stay in Ch.88; pure toy drones → Ch.95.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: appliances in heading 9021 that are NOT (i) for preventing/correcting bodily deformities OR (ii) for supporting/holding body parts following illness/operation/injury — and orthopaedic footwear/insoles failing the made-to-measure or singly-presented criteria
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purpose of heading 9021, the expression 'orthopaedic appliances' means appliances for: (i) preventing or correcting bodily deformities; or (ii) supporting or holding parts of the body following an illness, operation or injury. Orthopedic appliances include footwear and special insoles designed to correct orthopaedic conditions, provided that they are either (1) made to measure, or (2) mass produced, presented singly and not in pairs and designed to fit either foot equally.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression X means' with closed 2-purpose gate AND a closed sub-gate for footwear (must be made-to-measure OR mass-produced-singly). Ordinary footwear → Ch.64.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: automatic-control instruments in heading 9032 that do NOT (a) automatically control flow/level/pressure/temperature of liquids/gases by feedback-measure-correct OR (b) automatically regulate electrical quantities/non-electrical-via-electrical by feedback-measure-correct
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 9032 applies only to: (a) instruments and apparatus for automatically controlling the flow, level, pressure or other variables of liquids or gases, or for automatically controlling temperature, whether or not their operation depends on an electrical phenomenon which varies according to the factor to be automatically controlled, which are designed to bring this factor to, and maintain it at, a desired value, stabilized against disturbances, by constantly or periodically measuring its actual value; and (b) automatic regulators of electrical quantities, and instruments or apparatus for automatically controlling non-electrical quantities the operation of which depends on an electrical phenomenon varying according to the factor to be controlled, which are designed to bring this factor to, and maintain it at, a desired value, stabilized against disturbances, by constantly or periodically measuring its actual value.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with closed 2-class list. Manual valves, switches, simple thermostats without feedback loop → other Ch.84/85/90 headings.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: watches in heading 9101 whose case is NOT wholly of precious metal or precious-metal-clad metal, or those combined with pearls/precious/semi-precious stones; AND watches with base-metal case inlaid with precious metal
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: Heading 9101 covers only watches with case wholly of precious metal or of metal clad with precious metal, or of the same materials combined with natural or cultured pearls, or precious or semi-precious stones (natural, synthetic or reconstructed) of headings 7101 to 7104. Watches with case of base metal inlaid with precious metal fall in heading 9102.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Covers only' with closed material list AND explicit in-text redirect for base-metal-inlaid → 9102. Steel/plastic watches → 9102. Common false-anchor trap addressed.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: devices in Ch.91 marketed as 'watch movements' that exceed 12mm thickness or 50mm width/length/diameter, OR that lack a regulator system (balance-wheel, quartz, etc.) capable of determining intervals of time
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression 'watch movements' means devices regulated by a balance-wheel and hairspring, quartz crystal or any other system capable of determining intervals of time, with a display or a system to which a mechanical display can be incorporated. Such watch movements shall not exceed 12 mm in thickness and 50 mm in width, length or diameter.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression X means' with closed regulator-type list AND quantitative dimensional gate. Larger movements → clock movements (other Ch.91 headings) or general timing devices (Ch.84/85/90).

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: knots or tufts in heading 9603 that are MOUNTED (already incorporated into broom/brush bodies) OR that need significant further processing beyond minor top-trimming
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: In heading 9603, the expression 'prepared knots and tufts for broom or brush making' applies only to unmounted knots and tufts of animal hair, vegetable fibre or other material, which are ready for incorporation without division in brooms or brushes, or which require only such further minor processes as trimming to shap at the top, to render them ready for such incorporation.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'Applies only to' with 2-condition gate (unmounted + ready-for-incorporation). Mounted brushes are finished articles → also 9603 but different sub-line. Internal Ch.96 sub-classification.

proposed_inserts.excluded_product_text: engravings/prints/lithographs in heading 9702 produced by MECHANICAL or PHOTOMECHANICAL processes (i.e., not directly by hand by the artist)
proposed_inserts.source_note_text: For the purposes of heading 9702, the expression 'original engravings, prints and lithographs' means impressions produced directly, in black and white, or in colour, of one or of several plates wholly executed by hand by the artist, irrespective of the process or of the material employed by him, but not including any mechanical or photomechanical process.
proposed_inserts.rationale: 'The expression X means' with closed hand-made gate AND explicit exclusion of mechanical/photomechanical reproductions. Machine-printed reproductions → Ch.49 (printed pictures).
